text: Katharine Ellen Sykes OBE FInstP CPhys (born 20 December 1966) is a British physicist, broadcaster, and Professor of Sciences and Society at the University of Bristol. She previously held the position of Collier Professor of Public Engagement in Science and Engineering from 2002 to 2006. She has presented numerous BBC2 and Open University TV series, including Rough Science, Ever Wondered about Food, Alternative Therapies, and Alternative Medicine, and appeared in the documentary television miniseries Brave New World with Stephen Hawking in 2011. Sykes was educated at Fitzharrys School, a co-educational comprehensive school in Abingdon, and earned a Bachelor of Science degree in Physics from the University of Bristol in 1989, followed by a PhD in 1996, which focused on the crystallization and degradation of polyhydroxybutyrate, a biodegradable plastic. She helped create and co-directs the Cheltenham Science Festival and Famelab, a national UK competition that identifies and trains emerging talent in science communication. She served as Head of Science for Explore-At-Bristol, leading the team responsible for the content of the award-winning Hands-on Science Centre. Sykes is a member of the Council for Science and Technology (CST), the UK government's top-level advisory body on science and technology policy, and has served on advisory panels for public engagement in science with the Royal Society, the Wellcome Trust, and the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC). She is a trustee of NESTA and a board member of Explore-At-Bristol. In 2006, she received the Kohn Award for excellence in public engagement with science. She was awarded an honorary Doctor of Science degree and honorary fellowship from the University of Gloucestershire and won the Suffrage Science award in 2013. Sykes was appointed a Member of the Order of the British Empire (OBE) in the 2009 Birthday Honours.
